items.quantity: World total generation 2024 (TWh): Ember old long format vs new format
items.comment: Same publisher, two download formats. The older long-format file is 0.5% lower than the July-2026-format file (a revision between releases); prefer the new format for generation, capacity and emissions. The new format has no demand series, so ember_electricity_world still takes demand from the older file.

items.quantity: Data-centre share of world electricity, 2024 (%)
items.comment: The IEA's 1.5% rests on its own denominator (about 27,700 TWh implied); Ember's world demand (generation plus net imports, 30,912 TWh) is larger, which gives 1.3%. A scope difference in the denominator, not an error in either.

items.quantity: Power: Epoch's 95 tracked frontier AI data centres (current MW) vs the IEA's average load implied by 415 TWh a year (MW)
items.comment: Different scope and date: the IEA figure is the average load of all data centres in 2024; Epoch's is the power of 95 large AI sites in late 2026. The ratio (about 0.3) says tracked frontier sites already reach roughly a third of the IEA's 2024 global average data-centre load, not that either is wrong.

items.quantity: US data-centre electricity: LBNL 2023 vs IEA 2024 (TWh)

a.source: lbnl_dc_2024 (text: 176 TWh by 2023, 4.4% of US electricity)

items.comment: Different years (IEA 2024 vs LBNL 2023). LBNL reports 176 TWh in 2023 (4.4% of US electricity); the IEA reports about 180 TWh in 2024 (more than 4%). LBNL projects 325 to 580 TWh in 2028, i.e. growth of 13% to 27% a year from 2023 (computed here from its text), so a 2024 value only 2% above 2023 is at odds with its own trajectory: the two use different scope or method. They agree at the order of magnitude, not to better than about 20%.

items.quantity: World fossil CO2 emissions 2023 (Mt CO2): Global Carbon Budget 2025 vs Our World in Data
items.comment: OWID's world CO2 is built on the Global Carbon Project; they should agree to rounding (OWID may include cement carbonation, which GCB reports separately).

items.quantity: World CO2 emissions 2023 (Mt CO2): Global Carbon Budget 2025 fossil vs CEDS v_2025_03_18 total
items.comment: CEDS is a bottom-up inventory scaled to energy statistics; it includes cement process CO2 and international shipping and aviation. A small gap is expected.

items.quantity: World fossil CO2 2024 (Mt CO2): Global Carbon Budget 2025 vs EDGAR/IEA
items.comment: EDGAR values are CC BY-NC-ND, so only the relative difference is stored.

items.quantity: WDI EN.GHG.CO2.MT.CE.AR5 world 2024 vs EDGAR fossil CO2 2024
items.comment: The World Bank indicator is the EDGAR (IEA-EDGAR) series: the two world totals agree to the digits shown. Because EDGAR states those CO2 data are CC BY-NC-ND, the WDI series is excluded from the derived world file.

items.quantity: World methane 2023 (Mt CH4): EDGAR (CO2eq / 28, GWP-100 AR5) vs CEDS
items.comment: EDGAR includes wildfire/biomass sectors differently; both are anthropogenic inventories.

items.quantity: World population 2023: WPP 2024 (1 July) vs World Bank WDI
items.comment: WDI's population comes from several sources including WPP; mid-year vs year-end conventions explain small gaps.

items.quantity: World population 2024: WPP 2024 (1 July) vs World Bank WDI
items.comment: WDI's population comes from several sources including WPP; mid-year vs year-end conventions explain small gaps.

items.quantity: World cereal yield 2023 (kg/ha): FAOSTAT 'Cereals, primary' vs WDI AG.YLD.CREL.KG
items.comment: WDI uses FAO data but its 'cereals' aggregate excludes some items (for example it covers wheat, rice, maize, barley, oats, rye, millet, sorghum and mixed grains); differences of about 1% are definitional.

items.quantity: Cross-country median labour share 2019 (%): PWT 11.0 labsh x 100 vs ILO SDG 10.4.1
items.comment: Different definitions and samples (PWT adjusts for self-employed income and covers 100-140 countries; the ILO series is modelled for about 185 countries); a gap of several percentage points is expected. Neither is 'the' labour share.

items.quantity: Largest 2025 training run: Epoch AI notable models vs OWID series (FLOP)
items.comment: OWID's chart is a processed copy of the Epoch data set; the gap is the data vintage (the OWID export predates Epoch's latest update) and any filtering to the 'notable' list.
